chunks.title: Who Kaushik is
chunks.text: Kaushik Das is an AI engineer based in London, UK. He designs and ships end-to-end intelligence: RAG over clinical documents, voice agents on LiveKit, MCP toolchains, and sustainability-aware ML experiments. He cares about reliability, latency budgets and human-centered UX. He has 6+ years of engineering experience and has shipped production AI on 3 platforms. He holds an MSc in Artificial Intelligence from the University of Aberdeen.

chunks.title: What he works on now
chunks.text: Recent work spans multi-provider LLM orchestration, EEG-based Alzheimer's signal analysis, and computation-aware ML with sustainability metrics. His current focus is building production agentic AI: tool-calling LLM agents with deterministic safety boundaries, grounded analytics, and the forecasting models underneath them.

chunks.title: Collaboration and availability
chunks.text: Kaushik is open to collaborating on research aligned with applied LLMs, retrieval, or healthcare decision support, especially projects that value evals, transparency and real-world impact. He is interested in AI research collaboration and in discussing projects. The best way to reach him is email at kaushikdas.career@gmail.com.

chunks.title: How to contact him
chunks.text: Email: kaushikdas.career@gmail.com. His GitHub, LinkedIn and downloadable resume are all linked in the Contact section at the bottom of this site. Email is the most reliable route.

chunks.title: EY — Senior Consultant, AI Engineer (current)
chunks.text: Since September 2026, Kaushik is a Senior Consultant and AI Engineer at EY in London, United Kingdom. This is his current full-time role.

chunks.title: Aspect — AI Engineer (Mar 2026 to Sep 2026)
chunks.text: At Aspect in London (March 2026 to September 2026, full-time on-site) Kaushik was an Artificial Intelligence Engineer. He owned the AI layer of Chumley, an internal marketing-and-operations platform: an analytics chatbot over 78 tools, an AI pilot that plans Google Ads changes through a guarded write path, and the forecasting models underneath them. The changes the pilot plans now drive 30% of all new customer generation. Headline numbers: 30% of new customer generation, 3 production LLM agents, 78 tools in a single agent, 48% fewer prompt tokens, 20% lower holdout error.

chunks.title: Aspect — the three production agents
chunks.text: Kaushik built the analytics chatbot at the centre of Chumley on a custom tool-calling loop with no framework. Its 78 tools cover the system end to end — campaigns, spend, leads, jobs, Salesforce records and forecasts — so a question about any part of the business has a tool that can answer it rather than a model inferring it from context. He wrote the orchestration layer that works out which of those tools a question needs, and the agentic loop around it: the agent calls a tool, reads what came back and decides whether that answers the question or whether it needs to go again, chaining calls until the answer is resolved instead of stopping at the first plausible result. A separate presentation layer shapes the reply to what was asked, so the same underlying result arrives as a table, a comparison, a trend or a short narrative rather than always as prose. On top of it sits an AI pilot that plans the Google Ads work itself — reading current state, proposing a coherent multi-change plan for human review and handing it to the one guarded write path; the changes it plans now drive 30% of all new customer generation. Alongside them a per-campaign investigator produces entity-level to-do lists and then tracks whether each item was actually actioned.

chunks.title: Aspect — the safety model
chunks.text: He designed the safety model around a closed candidate space: deterministic code decides what changes are possible and computes every number, while the LLM may only select, sequence and narrate. A hallucinating model therefore degrades output instead of corrupting it, and no agent has its own write path. The grounding layer follows the principle that code does the arithmetic and the model narrates, with every total and ratio precomputed and verified. That came after the first verifier proved an over-broad allow-list is indistinguishable from no verification.

chunks.title: Aspect — cost and token work
chunks.text: He cut LLM cost through measurement rather than guesswork: a deterministic lexical tool router reduced prompt tokens by 48% with full recall on a 17-case suite, and restructuring the investigator's context cut its input tokens by 62%.

chunks.title: Aspect — statistical models in production
chunks.text: Statistical models he shipped at Aspect: conformal-band lead forecasting; a hurdle logistic plus Gamma GLM job-value model with empirical-Bayes effects, giving a 20% reduction in median holdout error; quantile completion-time bands; and a Poisson spend-to-leads model. He also shipped one model as 'measured, does not help' rather than serve a ranking built on noise.

chunks.title: Aspect — data correctness and reliability
chunks.text: He found and fixed systemic correctness failures in the data layer: campaign geography inferred from names rather than real targeting data, a nightly mirror that silently drifted, and a feature flag detected by string-matching that was wrong for 61 of 64 cases. He established the reliability layer from scratch: a structured error contract replacing endpoints that returned HTTP 200 with an error inside, an incident ledger, and deduplicated alerting segmented by impact.

chunks.title: PrecisionForward — AI Application Engineer (Jun 2025 to Mar 2026)
chunks.text: At PrecisionForward in Scotland, United Kingdom (June 2025 to March 2026, full-time remote), Kaushik was an AI Application Engineer. He led the build of an agentic platform for search engine optimisation that treats large language models as a search surface in their own right: agents run an organisation's real customer questions against 4 LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude and Grok) and record, for each answer, whether the brand is named, how it is characterised and which competitor is named instead. The platform turns that into AI visibility optimisation, attributing each absence to a cause the client can act on (no citable source, thin coverage of the question, a competitor owning the phrasing) and specifying the content and structuring work that closes it. Visibility is measured region by region, because the same question asked from different markets returns different brands, so organisations can prioritise by market. Underneath it he built a RAG retrieval layer over brand, competitor and source material with semantic Elasticsearch embeddings, so every finding is traceable to the passage it came from, and orchestrated the four providers behind one interface with per-provider prompt handling and normalised outputs. Separately at PrecisionForward he built a hospital discharge assistant pairing structured ML (XGBoost) with GPT-4o for 30-day readmission prediction and discharge-readiness scoring, human-in-the-loop throughout. Much of that work was data preparation: reconciling inconsistent clinical coding across sources, imputing and flagging missing observations rather than dropping the row, collapsing duplicate patient histories, treating outliers on clinical rather than statistical grounds, and drawing train/test splits per patient so no prior admission leaked across the boundary. Its retrieval used Elasticsearch and sentence-transformer embeddings for metadata-aware document understanding, with synthetic data generation and ETL pipelines to work around low-resource clinical datasets. The role covered team leadership, LLM systems and cloud architecture.

chunks.title: Digital Technology Partner — Gen AI Developer (Sep 2024 to Jul 2025)
chunks.text: At Digital Technology Partner in Glasgow (September 2024 to July 2025, contract, remote), Kaushik was a Gen AI Developer. He built a financial RAG pipeline over insurance claim and incident records: documents chunked, embedded and held in a vector database and retrieved by semantic search, so a claims handler could ask a question in plain English and get an answer with the source passages attached. He used it for pattern recognition across claim histories, surfacing which incidents cluster by season, site and cause — National Rail's winter weather and track incidents and the North Sea oil rigs' own seasonal profile both read as recurring, predictable exposure rather than unrelated events, letting underwriting anticipate the peak. The same patterns drive fraud prevention: claims sitting outside the established seasonal, geographic and causal profile are flagged for investigation, so assessors review genuine outliers instead of sampling the whole book. He also made cause explainable — given a new incident the pipeline retrieves its closest historical matches and returns the contributing factors those cases shared, with records cited. The pipeline is automated end to end with webhooks triggering ingestion, embedding and indexing as new claims land, behind data guardrails that validate each record on the way in and quarantine what fails rather than letting a malformed batch silently degrade retrieval.

chunks.title: Kairos Consulting — Software Engineer (Jul 2019 to Dec 2022)
chunks.text: At Kairos Consulting in Kolkata, India (July 2019 to December 2022, full-time), Kaushik did computer vision R&D with OpenCV and Keras/TensorFlow, focused on optimisation and Dockerised production deployments. He contributed to a healthcare R&D project on real-time image processing using OpenCV and Scikit-Image for noise reduction, contrast enhancement and feature extraction; achieved a 15% improvement in anomaly detection accuracy with CNNs; optimised FFT and PCA routines with NumPy and SciPy; and increased sales 23% via a Random Forest demand-forecasting model. Stack included AWS EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Docker and CI/CD.

chunks.title: MSc Artificial Intelligence, University of Aberdeen
chunks.text: Kaushik completed an MSc in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Aberdeen, UK, from 2023 to 2024, with a GPA of 15.6 out of 22. He was a recipient of the Scottish Government Postgraduate Scholarship. Coursework covered Machine Learning, Deep Learning, NLP and Computer Vision. Aberdeen was ranked 208th QS World 2023, 29th QS UK 2023 and 21st QS Sustainability, and founded in 1495 it is the 5th-oldest university in the English-speaking world.

chunks.title: BTech Electronics & Communication, IEM Kolkata
chunks.text: Kaushik holds a BTech in Electronics and Communication Engineering from IEM, Kolkata (MAKAUT), India, 2015 to 2019, with a CGPA of 7.34 out of 10, focused on signal processing and embedded systems, and telecommunications. At the time MAKAUT was a degree-awarding university in the NIRF Engineering 151-200 band with NAAC A accreditation; the institute was established in 1989.

chunks.title: Project: Chumley — AI Campaign Operations
chunks.text: Chumley (Aspect, 2026) is a FastAPI and React platform sitting between Google Ads, Salesforce and the business. It carries an analytics chatbot over 78 tools, an orchestration layer picking the right tool and an agentic loop chaining calls until the question resolves, a presentation layer shaping each reply to what was asked, and an AI pilot planning Google Ads changes on top. Exactly one guarded code path may write, with every change human-approved and ledgered. Forecasting, capacity and job-value models sit underneath. The pilot's plans drive 30% of new customer generation. Live at chumley.ai.

chunks.title: Project: AI Search & Insight Platform
chunks.text: Built at PrecisionForward in 2025: an agentic platform measuring whether a brand is named when customers ask an LLM. Real customer questions are run against GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude and Grok per market, and each absence is attributed to a cause the client can fix. RAG over brand and competitor sources with Elasticsearch embeddings; FastAPI backend hosted on Azure with low latency, evals and observability. Live at precisionfwd.com.

chunks.title: Project: Hospital Discharge Assistant
chunks.text: Built at PrecisionForward in 2025: XGBoost readmission prediction fused with GPT-4o reasoning for discharge-readiness scoring. The work that decided whether it held up sat upstream of the model — raw admission records reconciled across inconsistent clinical coding, missing observations imputed and flagged rather than dropped with the row, duplicate patient histories collapsed, and splits drawn per patient so no prior admission leaked across the train/test boundary. Semantic retrieval on Elasticsearch and sentence-transformer embeddings on top. Live at precisionfwd.com.

chunks.title: Project: Hospital Agent Platform
chunks.text: A personal Portia-based project from 2025: a human-in-the-loop agent running transcript intake, triage, approvals and actions. Uses ChromaDB, encrypted IPFS transcripts and Azure OpenAI for safe, auditable decisions. Source on GitHub.

chunks.title: Project: EEG Alzheimer's Detection
chunks.text: A 2024 research prototype, DST-SERB funded: early Alzheimer's detection via EEG feature pipelines and ML classification, with signal processing and an evaluation dashboard.

chunks.title: Project: Sustainability-Aware ML
chunks.text: Independent research from 2024: a computation-aware pipeline tracking CO2, runtime and instability across models including XGBoost and LightGBM. It introduced Green ROI and TOPSIS scoring to balance performance against cost and emissions. Paper in progress. Uses CodeCarbon.

chunks.title: Project: Medical Chatbot (PIXTRAL)
chunks.text: Built for the Mistral AI Hack UK in September 2024, where it was a finalist: PIXTRAL-12B with RAG on NHS datasets, session context, prompt chaining and safety fallback rules. Listed on Devpost.

chunks.title: Project: Privacy-Centric Skin Classifier
chunks.text: Built for the META Hackathon in October 2024: encrypted inference via zero-knowledge proofs and multi-party computation, with IPFS for tamper-proof storage, producing certifiable outputs without exposing raw patient data.

chunks.title: Hackathons
chunks.text: Mistral AI Hack UK, London, September 2024: finalist among 200+ teams with a medical chatbot using PIXTRAL-12B and RAG grounded on NHS datasets, with session memory, safety fallback rules and automated prompt chaining. META Hackathon, online, October 2024: encrypted inference using ZKP and MPC with IPFS tamper-proof storage for privacy-preserving skin disease classification. Brave x Nebius x Cerebral Valley, London, 2022: early exploration of RAG-based chat, building a working demo of multi-step prompt chaining with retrieval grounding using Brave search and open-source LLMs.

chunks.title: Research interests
chunks.text: Kaushik's research interests sit at the intersection of LLM systems, retrieval quality, computer vision, NLP and healthcare AI. Especially reinforcement learning, retrieval-augmented generation over clinical and scientific corpora, agent workflows with human-in-the-loop decision making, and evaluation frameworks balancing accuracy, transparency and efficiency. Related areas: YOLO, AI/ML/RL, sustainable ML, RAG and A2A.

chunks.title: Awards and recognition
chunks.text: Kaushik is a Scottish Government Postgraduate Scholarship recipient, a Mistral AI Hackathon finalist, and a DST-SERB collaboration researcher.

chunks.title: Skills and stack
chunks.text: Technologies Kaushik has shipped with, as evidenced across his roles and projects: Python, FastAPI, React; LLM orchestration across GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Mistral and Azure OpenAI; tool-calling agents and MCP toolchains; RAG with Elasticsearch, ChromaDB and sentence-transformer embeddings; LiveKit voice agents; classical and statistical ML with XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, GLMs, conformal prediction and Poisson models; computer vision with OpenCV, Keras, TensorFlow, Scikit-Image and YOLO; NumPy, SciPy; AWS (EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront) and Azure; Docker and CI/CD; IPFS, ZKP and MPC for privacy-preserving inference; CodeCarbon for emissions tracking.
